articleTitle: Numerical investigation of local field bow wave by AMR_based CFD method
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Bow wave is generally associated with the breaking wave phenomenon, which has attracted much attentions. To figure out the mechanism and the relationship between local field bow wave and wave breaking phenomenon, numerical simulation is conducted by CFD (computational fluid dynamic) with the introduction of UAMR (user defined adaptive mesh refinement). Before the analyses of the flow field, relevant validations are initially carried out. With validated flow field, local field bow is investigated by velocity vector analysis, where the discontinuity of the flow beneath bow wave is observed. Based on Q-criteria vortex recognition method, vortex motion towards downstream wake field is clearly discovered. Velocity head loss contour, of which the distribution range exceeds the ship width, further proves the momentum loss evolution from nonlinear bow wave. Therefore, the energy translation of nonlinear bow wave is confirmed in the nonlinear bow wave. Considering no obvious wave breaking phenomenon is observed in present simulation, nonlinear properties instead of breaking phenomenon itself should be the most important feature in local field bow wave. The present research could be helpful for further understanding the physical mechanism of local field bow wave and their contribution to total resistance.

articleTitle: Design and acoustic performance analysis of acoustic black hole silencer
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Acoustic black hole(ABH) has the advantages of high efficiency, light weight, and wide frequency, which can be used for duct noise reduction in industrial equipment. The influence of ABH structural parameters on acoustic performance is analysed through calculating the theoretical solution of the reflection coefficients of linear and quadratic ABH waveguides. By combining the ABH duct with a resistance silencer, an ABH duct embedded in the expansion cavity silencer was designed, and the noise reduction performance of the composite silencer was simulated and analyzed. The results indicate that the ABH silencer has better noise reduction performance than a simple expansion cavity silencer. The position of the intake pipe affects the low-frequency transmission loss, while the position of the exhaust pipe only changes the transmission loss in the mid-frequency range. The length of exhaust pipe has little effect on transmission loss. Increasing the length of the expansion chamber is beneficial for low-frequency sound absorption.

articleTitle: Numerical investigation of velocity on local scour below subsea pipeline in steady flow
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Local scour below a subsea pipeline is investigated numerically for gap ratios (e0/D) -0.3 to 0.1 and shield parame-ter to critical shield parameter ratio ranging from θ/θc 0.3 to 1.49. The positive and negative gap ratio represent that the pipeline is above and below (sagged into) the undisturbed flat sand surface, respectively. The aim of this study is to investi-gate the effect of Shields parameter ratio on the scour development. Shear stress transport (SST) k-ω turbulence equations, sediment transport rates, and Reynolds-Averaged Navier Stokes (RANS) equations are solved to simulate the flow. It is found that the scour depth increases nearly with the increase of the Shields parameter ratio in the clear water regime (Shields parameter is less than 1). In the live bed regime, the Shields parameter does not have effect on the scour depth. This study further found that lowering pipeline position increases the scour depth in the live bed condition but does not change the scour depth much in the clear water condition.

articleTitle: Experimental study on punching performance of RC two-way slabs composite strengthened with CFRP
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The resistance to punching shear of reinforced concrete (RC) two-way slabs composite strengthened with carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) was investigated. The failure mode, load-deformation curve and the bearing capacity of the specimen were analysed. The test results demonstrated that the load capacity of the specimen increased nonlinearly with the increase number of CFRP. The strengthened technique provided in this study can delay crack propagation, improve the punching shear load capacity and significantly increase their stiffness after cracking compared with standard slabs. It is concluded that the compo-site strengthened technique for RC two-way slabs in this paper is feasible. The strengthened effect of the combination of CFRP bars and CFRP plates is optimal.

articleTitle: Research on a parameterized design method for medium and high-speed catamaran
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: In recent years, renewable energy such as wind energy is used more widely. China has abundant offshore wind energy resources, and the wind farm service vessels are used frequently. Catamaran is suitable for wind farm service because of its large deck area and excellent seakeeping, so there is a great de-mand from shipowners. In this paper, a parameterized geometry design method and a resistance evaluation flow-process based on potential flow for medium and high-speed catamaran were proposed. Using this method, A twin-hull me-dium and high-speed wind farm service vessel with the length of 20m was de-signed. The main characteristic parameters of the hull were optimized quickly, and a hull with excellent performance was obtained. The resistance perfor-mance of the optimized hull was verified through model tests and meets the requirement of speed indicators. It is suggested that the parameterized design method proposed in this paper can be generalized and applied, it will greatly reduce the design cycle and cost of this vessels.

articleTitle: Research on the impact resistance characteristics of ship side structure obstacle grid particle dampers
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: To address the issue of blank applications of particle damping for ship impact resistance, a theoretical model for the vibration reduction principle of obstacle grid particle dampers was developed based on the Hertz contact theory. A novel type of obstacle grid particle damper was designed. In order to verify the effectiveness and superiority of obstacle grid particle dampers in resisting impact and analysed the similarities and differences with traditional particle dampers, a numerical model of particle dampers with built-in obstacle grids was established using the discrete element method. Experimental verification was conducted to study the in-fluence of obstacle grids on the impact resistance performance of the damper. The results showed that under conditions of 55g half-sine impact vibration and 50%filling ratio, obstacle grids could improve certain characteristics of traditional particle dampers.

articleTitle: Simulation of high speed water entry with gas kinetics scheme
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Based on Gas Kinetics Scheme (GKS), the numerical simulation of high speed water entry is studied. In the process of the object entering water from the air at high speed, and the phenomenon of transmedium motion and cavitation occurs, involving two phases and three media of gas/vapor/water. In this paper, a two-phase and three-media compressible cavitation flow solver is developed, in which the gas/vapor/water are compressible and can effectively deal with the interaction between different media. In this paper, vertical entry into water of axisymmetric cylinder with flat head and 45° cone head is calculated. The calculation is simplified by axisymmetric method. This method can predict the generation, propagation and local high pressure induced by shock wave in the flow field, and then obtain the instantaneous load when the object enters the water. The cylinder generates a shock wave when entering the water, and gradually spreads to the distance. The intensity of the shock wave generated by the flat-head cylinder is much greater than that of the cone-head cylinder, and the cavity generated by entering the water will wrap the cylinder completely. A flat-head cylinder creates a larger cavity and exerts more pressure on its head, so the cylinder experiences greater resistance. Due to the very short time of water entry, cavitation almost did not occur in the early stage of water entry, and it was difficult to observe obvious cavitation. This study provides a reference for GKS method to study high-speed water entry motion.

articleTitle: Analysis of cutting resistance of single rake tooth in saturated clay and unsaturated clay
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: It is a common method of dredging engineering to use a rake suction vessel to dig sand and extract clay. Aiming at the cutting problem, the CEL finite element method is used to study the interaction between the cutter teeth and clay. And the relationship between the cutting resistance and the moving displacement of the cutter teeth is obtained. The feasibility and accuracy of the numerical method to analyze the problem of cutting clay with the cutter was verified. Furthermore, the influence of the clay modulus of elasticity, cutting angle, cutting speed and cutting depth on the cutting resistance limit was quantitatively analyzed for the saturated and unsaturated clay. And the influence degree of the above cutting parameters was discussed. The results show that the cutting resistance limit in horizontal direction increases with the increase of clay modulus of elasticity, cutting angle and cutting depth. And the difference between the cutting resistance limit in saturated clay and unsaturated clay increases with the increase of the above parameters. The cutting resistance limit in the vertical direction basically increases with the increase of clay modulus of elasticity and cutting depth, and then increases inversely with the increase of cutting angle. Moreover, with the increase of cutting depth, the difference between the cutting resistance limit values of saturated clay and unsaturated clay becomes larger. In addition, the cutting resistance limit in saturated clay is basically unchanged with the increase of cutting speed, while the cutting resistance limit in unsaturated clay is basically increasing with the increase of cutting speed. These results can provide beneficial reference for subsequent engineering application.

articleTitle: Drag reduction effect of micro-vortex on the surface of imitated shark skin
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Surface frictional drag significantly impacts the performance of marine equipment, leading to increased energy consumption, reduced sailing speed, and potential equipment damage. As widely known, sharks, among the fastest fish in the ocean, possess skin covered with numerous tiny and dense scales. This paper simplified the scale structure of shark skin into four different patterned surfaces: lines, discontinuous lines, equal gradient riblet, and graded riblet. The flow field near these patterned surfaces was analyzed under both vertical and parallel flow conditions. It was observed that the drag reduction effect varied with the flow direction and patterned structure. Notably, the graded riblet exhibited an excellent drag reduction effect. This finding suggests a promising avenue for improving the efficiency of marine equipment.

articleTitle: Comparison and evaluation of cruise atrium theme design
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Cruise ship is a large building for water navigation. The cruise atrium is the most critical node of the cruise ship public space and the transportation hub connecting horizontal and vertical transportation. Every cruise ship has a specific theme, which is related to the brand positioning of the cruise company, the culture of the starting point and the destination of the route, etc. As the first stop for visitors to board the ship, the interior design of the atrium is often designed gorgeously according to the cruise theme, aiming to bring visitors novel experience and direction guidance. This paper takes the atrium of China's first self-built large cruise ship as the research object, innovatively combines space narrative and space syntax to evaluate its three interior decoration designs. These three designs for the same cruise ship atrium have very different themes, and the expected space experience for visitors is also very different. Firstly, the space narrative analysis of these three designs is carried out from the three elements of narrative: objects, scenes, and events. These three designs for the same cruise ship atrium have very different themes, and the expected space experience for visitors is also very different. In addition, Depthmap, a space syntax software, was used to analyse the connection and visual integration of each layer, to quantitatively evaluate the spatial experience effect of the atrium thematic design. Through comparative analysis, the advantages and disadvantages of the design were found, and optimization suggestions were put forward for the design that affected traffic and weakened the spatial experience effect.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of the hydrodynamics of a uniformly moving underwater vehicle by internal waves
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: This paper analyzes and determines the optimal navigation speed by investigating the characteristics of hydrodynamic load changes caused by different velocities as the underwater vehicle passes through the internal waves. The underwater vehicle model is chosen as a slender body model, and the outflow field is generated by the overset grid method, and utilizing the velocity inlet wave creation approach to construct a numerical model depicting the impact of internal waves on the underwater vehicle. The results show that when the underwater vehicle passes through the internal wave at different speeds, Its healing and pitching forces have a great influence on the orientation of the study object.

articleTitle: Hydrodynamic performance verification and analysis of flexible floating breakwater
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Ships will be affected by the waves directly in the sea environment and the resistance of the ship increases when it is sailing in the waves. Meanwhile, if it has amphibious landing equipment out of the ship, it is difficult to operate. Therefore, it is necessary to arrange a flexible wave elimination system near the ship to improve flow, which is useful for releasing amphibious landing equipment. In this paper, the numerical simulation of a floating breakwater is carried out, and the simulation results are compared with the experimental data to verify the reliability of the present numerical model. We can conclude that the wave amplitude increases with the increase of the period while the wave height is constant. With the increase of the period, the wave elimination efficiency decreases obviously.

articleTitle: Numerical and experimental studies of ultimate strength of GFRP hat beams
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Composite materials in hull structures are becoming increasingly popular, but accurate prediction of their failure modes and ultimate strength remains a challenging issue. The hat beam made of glass fibre reinforced polymer (GFRP) with a foam core is a typical composite structure in ship continuous longitudinal structures. Two different types of GFRP hat beams, including longitudinal stiffeners and stringers, are selected as the objects of study. The ultimate strength of these hat beams under axial compression are investigated by various simulation methods, such as multilayer shell elements, multilayer solid elements, equivalent single layer shell elements and solid elements. Then, model experiments of these GFRP hat beams under longitudinal compression are performed to find the failure modes. The two structures exhibit different damage modes: the stringer shows yield damage, whereas the longitudinal stiffener occurs buckling and delaminates within the laminate. Based on the comparison of experimental and numerical results, it is demonstrated that the multilayer shell elements are simpler and also have a higher simulation accuracy in the calculation of the ultimate strength of such thin laminates. The conclusions in this paper will provide a guidance for the safety analysis of GFRP structures.

articleTitle: Review of torpedo detection, identification and warning technology research
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: At present, torpedoes seriously help the safety of underwater vehicles. In order to obtain more response time and space, the alarm of torpedo attack is very important. First of all, the torpedo alarm process is combed and introduced to deepen the understanding of torpedo alarm, multi-directional comprehensive analysis. Then, the research progress of torpedo attack alarm is analyzed, and the research progress is introduced form the aspects of target detection, signal processing, feature extraction and target recognition, so as to intuitively understand and understand the current situation. Finally, the development trend of torpedo alarm is described.

articleTitle: Hybrid gas and steam turbine power plant for FPSO vessel
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: New avenues for modern thermal engine production are emerging as challenges related to the enhancement of offshore gas turbine plants are addressed. The integration of gas and steam turbines in a hybrid cycle, utilizing a range of fuels such as hydrocarbons, pure hydrogen, and hydrogen-enriched gases, offers a diverse array of potential output characteristics. The primary objective of this research is to theoretically explore the characteristics of a combined gas and steam turbine power installation and evaluate its suitability for deployment in a floating production, storage, and offloading (FPSO) vessel. The study contemplates a potential and promising configuration for a combined gas and steam turbine power plant with a hybrid cycle. To attain efficient energy performance, a promising scheme has been suggested, incorporating gas turbine engines with different thermal circuits. This includes configurations both with and without the recovery of exhaust gas heat in the cycle of a contact installation, featuring steam injection into the burner device of the gas turbine. The objective of this research is to formulate technical solutions within the marine energy sector, specifically focusing on the development of decarbonized energy systems. The environmental performance of the hybrid plant is enhanced through the use of hydrogen as fuel. Optimization calculations affirm the plant's adaptability to adjust output parameters by altering the operational mode of a marine contact-type gas turbine engine.

articleTitle: Analysis of axial vibration characteristics of stepped lifting pipe in deep sea mining
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: During deep-sea mining operations, the stepped lifting pipe generates huge additional loads and significant dynamic displacements under the excitation of the mining vessel's heave motion, and its axial vibration is a highly dangerous behavior.In order to investigate the nonlinear dynamic behavior of a stepped lifting pipe system under external loads such as top disturbance excitation, waves, and ocean currents, this paper studies the axial vibration modes and vibration responses of the stepped pipe based on the theory of continuous elastic rod vibration and the ABAQUS finite element model. The results indicate that the influence of the buffer on the mass effect of the stepped pipe is more significant than its stiffness effect. As the seawater depth increases, the axial tension gradually decreases while the axial vibration displacement gradually increases. Moreover, the growth rate of longitudinal amplitude along the length of the stepped pipe is closely related to the frequency of top disturbance excitation. The closer the frequency of top disturbance excitation is to the stepped pipe's natural frequency, the faster the axial amplitude increases along the length of the pipeline. The findings of this paper can provide support for the safe and reliable design and prediction of the dynamic performance of lifting pipes.

articleTitle: Effect of height to width ratio on seismic performance of X-shaped diagonally braced foam concrete composite wall panel
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: In this paper, based on the stress cloud simulation results of ABAQUS, the X-shaped diagonally braced foam concrete composite wall panels were designed and fabricated, and by selecting the optimal test scheme, the static test proposed to take the aspect ratio as the only variable was carried out to comparatively an-alyse the differences in seismic performance of the two types of composite wall panels with the change of aspect ratio, such as the damage characteristics and the force mechanism. The X-shaped diagonally braced foam concrete compo-site wall panels designed and fabricated in this paper were applied to the as-sembled monolithic reinforced concrete frame-diagonal braced structure, where the diagonal braces within the wall panels divided the wall panels and changed them from symmetrical parallelograms to stable force triangles, which im-proved the displacement and deformation capacity of the structure as well as its ability to absorb seismic energy. The combined force of the diagonal bracing, infill panels and frame makes the seismic defence shape of the structure no longer monolithic and improves the strength, stiffness, ductility, energy dissipa-tion capacity and stability of the structure; it improves the force performance.

articleTitle: Embedded spool stiction and abnormal temperature elevation faults signals reconstruction based on experimental methods
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: As key control components in fluid power systems, solenoid on-off valves are widely used in heavy industry. Due to the high working frequency and complex working conditions, solenoid valves are prone to have faults, if not resolved in time, which will affect continuity of work or even safety. At present, the prevailing approaches rely on experience for troubleshooting after faults, which requires highly trained maintenance personnel with extensive experiences, making them difficult to detect minor faults early on. Recently, with the rapid development of machine learning, artificial intelligence has also been extensively applied to fault diagnosis in hydraulic components or system and demonstrated excellent results. However, the accuracies of the learnt models are heavily dependent upon the availability of data sets. Therefore, this article designs an embedded fault diagnosis test system that outputs valve spool displacement and coil temperature signals in normal or quantifiable states, emulating solenoid valve in various working conditions in real-time. The embedded fault feature extraction models are also developed for spool stiction and abnormal temperature elevation faults, providing an economically feasible real-time data generation platform for studying solenoid on-off valve faults.

articleTitle: A simulation tension prediction method developed for single-point mooring lines system using GBRTO -lstm-boosting ensemble algorithm
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The single-point mooring system model is established with Ansys software to research time-serial network algorithm prediction of simulation tension in complex ocean working condition. Calculate current load coefficient by mathematical empirical formulas and wind load coefficient with Isherwood method to solve the single-point mooring instantaneous simulation tension response under current wind wave combining environment loads. The long-short term memory (LSTM) neural network and the gradient boosting regression tree (GBRT) optimization and LSTM ensemble algorithm model (GBRTO-LSTM-Boosting) are set up to train and predict the simulation tension data set according to time sequence feature. The ensemble algorithm learns with method of renewing connection weights and dynamically connection parameters among base learners. Comparative and analysis the variation of the mooring lines tension and prediction results based on responses of single-point mooring lines system. The experimental results show that the mooring lines tension of single-point mooring lines system prediction evaluation indicators RMSE and MAPE reduce respectively by 31.74 and 0.014, R2 and Acc averagely improve by 0.008 and 0.026 and the time waste of training and prediction decreases by 12.11s after using GBRTO-LSTM-Boosting ensemble model, which proves that GBRTO-LSTM-Boosting algorithm model could work efficiently and predict simulation mooring lines tension better with some reference value in the process of mooring system design and prediction.

articleTitle: Influence of cut-off wall depth on seepage and stability of reservoir embankment
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The mechanism of the cut-off wall is to increase the length of the seepage path of the water inside the reservoir, reduce the hydraulic gradient of the water flow and therefore reducing the external seepage of the reservoir. However, the study of the influence of cut-off wall depth was rare. Thus, in this study, a series of three-dimensional (3D) numerical simulation tests were carried out to investigate the influence of depth of cut-off wall on seepage characteristics of reservoir and provide suggestions based on the site condition of Xinjizhou water supply project. The results revealed that for the condition of dry season, only the cut-off wall penetrated into the micro-permeable layer, the flow rate of the reservoir was greatly reduced and the cut-off effect was better. On the other hand, for the condition of wet season, with the increase of depth of the cut-off wall, the hydraulic gradient near the cut-off wall changed significantly, resulting in a significant decrease in the hydraulic gradient at the top of the reservoir slope, while the hydraulic gradient at the toe of the slope changed little. In order to meet the requirements of the safety factor, the depth of the anti-seepage wall based on the condition of Xinjizhou water supply project should be designed as at least 20 m.

articleTitle: On mixing performance of pre-mixing abrasive water jet chamber profiles
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The existing pre-mixing abrasive water jet does not control the mass fraction of abrasive at the outlet, and the research on the pre-mixing process is still lacking. In this paper, a pre-mixed abrasive water jet plane flow field test system based on image correlation method is constructed. A CCD camera that does not interfere with the flow field and can measure the global flow field is used to capture the mixing process, and visual image information is processed based on MATLAB to obtain the water and sand mixing information of the plane flow field. Finally, CFD software is used to simulate the internal plane flow field. The influence degree of the uniformity of the internal flow field on the shape of the plane flow field is compared. The influence of flow field shape on abrasive mass fraction at nozzle is analysed. Results have shown that the mixing uniformity of abrasive particles in convex-corned flow field is better than concave one under constant inlet velocity and pressure at the flow field. But preliminary results also indicate that convex-corned flow field may be have the highest abrasive fluctuations at the nozzle.

articleTitle: Instability mechanisms of pedestrians on compound slope dikes subject to excessive overtopping waves
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The new compound slope dikes are a category of environmentally beneficial hydraulic construction with features of green channel networking and coastal scenic tourism. However, extreme weather conditions such as tsunamis and typhoon surges will result in unusually raised sea levels and powerful non-linear waves that will seriously threaten the safety of buildings and vehicles on top of the dike and pedestrians on the observation terraces. In this paper, model experiments and numerical simulations based on an equivalent scale model were conducted on the basis of an actual accident, investigating the wave action processes of the forward thump and reverse recoil, and elaborating the interaction mechanisms between extreme waves and the pedestrian iso scale model. The accuracy of the numerical model was validated by comparing it with the experimental results. The results indicate that for various wave height conditions, the maximum reverse recoil force on the pedestrian above the platform is more pronounced compared to the head-on impulsive effect, which consequently results in the pedestrians being swept into the water.

articleTitle: Application of large tonnage square pontoon with shallow draft in sunken ship salvage
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: During the 13th Five-Year Plan period, our country's salvage equipment has developed significantly. The maximum lifting capacity of floating cranes has reached 12,000 ton, and the lifting capacity of tension jacks has reached 25,000 ton, which basically meets the external buoyancy requirements of 100,000-ton shipwreck salvage operations. However, in the salvage of sunken ships in extremely shallow waters, these heavy equipment could not work effectively due to water depth limitations. How to provide sufficient external buoyancy for sunken ships in extremely shallow waters has become a difficult problem in rescue. In this regard, this paper introduced an innovative idea. Based on the traditional ship salvage method by using steel pontoon, the bottom line of the circular cross section of the traditional pontoon was widened to make it a square pontoon structure, so that the square pontoon could obtain larger buoyancy at a lower draft. In addition, the paper also introduced the attention points in the design and practical application, so as to provide reference for the future use and research of the large tonnage pontoon.

articleTitle: Development of plasma-chemical combustion intensification systems for hydrocarbon fuels in marine power engineering
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The problem of efficient and environmentally friendly use of energy resources, as well as the rational consumption of expensive hydrocarbon fuels and fuel oils, is highly relevant to various types and purposes of marine power plants (MPP). Enhancing their efficiency requires the integration of modern advancements in science and technology into the design, engineering, and operation practices of vessels for various purposes. An important direction for improving MPP is the enhancement of fuel combustion device characteristics, such as combustion chambers of gas turbine and diesel engines, as well as steam generator furnaces. A new scientifically substantiated development in the field of marine power engineering has been successfully implemented. This development is based on the utilization of the proposed method of plasma-chemical combustion intensification, which provides a solution to this important problem in the maritime energy sector. This method relies on the interaction of a stream of low-temperature air plasma with organic fuel. As a result of the thermal, kinetic, and turbulent effects of the plasma-fuel torch, processes of vaporization, mixing, and oxidation of the primary fuel in the combustion chamber are intensified. Conducted research has confirmed the practical significance of fundamentally new schemes for organizing the working process in marine and stationary power engineering, based on plasma-chemical intensification of the preparation and combustion of fuels with different physical states.

articleTitle: Optimization of propeller hydrodynamic performance based on FDBSFS algorithm
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: In this work, an optimization design of marine propeller achieved using FDBSFS algorithm. The requirements for propulsion efficiency, cavitation, main engine power, and blade strength are taken into account in the optimization procedure. An interpolation fitting method based on triangulation is provided to fit the experimental data from wageningen pools in order to solve for the propeller hydrodynamic performance. The FDBSFS method effectively solves the premature convergence problem and provides superior exploration capabilities. In this study, the algorithm and genetic algorithm are both applied to the best propeller design. The analysis's findings indicate that the FDBSFS algorithm is more resilient and has an 88% faster rate of convergence than the genetic algorithm. When compared to the genetic algorithm, the FDBSFS method's accuracy is also somewhat improved. The propeller optimization design approach based on the FDBSFS algorithm significantly increases design efficiency when compared to the conventional propeller design method.

articleTitle: Study of the coupled dynamic response in a multi-body system for salvaging a large-tonnage shipwreck
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: When engaging in the retrieval of a shipwreck amidst the sea, the intricate operational milieu may incite the vessel to react vehemently. In this manuscript, a duo of hoisting barges has been employed to salvage a shipwreck weighing 11,700 tons at a water depth of 280 meters. The effects of different mooring modes on the lifting barges-lifting cables-shipwreck system are studied. Results of the research are as follows. The amplitude of motion exhibited by the barge that encounters the oncoming wave sur-passes, by a certain margin, that observed in the barge positioned on the opposing side. The mooring cables ought to be interconnected in a symmetrical radial pat-tern encircling the barge. Mooring cables should be arranged transversely (i.e., along the width of the ship) encircling the barge, thereby yielding substantial enhancement in the system's stability. The zenith value of tension exhibited by the lifting cables manifests a distribution akin to a "middle part drooping" pattern along the longitudinal span of the ship. The lifting barges-lifting cables-shipwreck system studied in this manuscript can provide a reference for the actual salvage operation.

articleTitle: Simulation and experimental investigation of acoustic performance of air valves in cruise ship air conditioning systems
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: This study investigates the impact of air conditioning systems on cruise ships, specifically focusing on the air valves, with a particular emphasis on vibration and noise. By utilizing advanced computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and Lighthill calculation methods, both simulations and experimental research were conducted. The results highlight significant differences in aerodynamic noise levels, depending on the angle at which the air valves are opened. Interestingly, the minimum noise was observed when the valve was fully open at a 90° angle, although this configuration was found to be susceptible to flutter phenomena. The dominant source of low-frequency aerodynamic noise was identified as the fan blade and shaft frequencies. Additionally, low-frequency noise from pipe radiation showed minimal attenuation, leading to a substantial amount of low-frequency noise energy persisting. These research findings are of great value as they provide insights into the design and implementation of air valves in cruise ship air conditioning systems to effectively reduce aerodynamic noise.

articleTitle: Research on frequency domain method of multiaxial random vibration fatigue life prediction based on critical plane method
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: It is necessary to traverse the entire random loading process, resulting in low computational efficiency and prediction accuracy to predict fatigue life. Considering this scenario, a frequency domain approach is presented for predicting the life of structure. The method is based on the critical plane, which is determined using the stress criterion. By treating the multi-axial stress state as equivalent to uniaxial stress. Once the equivalent strain or stress is derived, further analysis can be conducted to assess the fatigue life. The life of structure is obtained by combining the formula of the life prediction of the method. The research provides an efficient multi-axis random fatigue life prediction method. Compared with the traditional method, the prediction accuracy is higher and the workload is greatly reduced. It provides theoretical support for multi-axis random vibration fatigue life analysis of key components of marine diesel engines.

articleTitle: Analysis on coupling static magnetic field of underwater electric dipole
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: By the means of analytic expression of underwater electric dipole's coupling static magnetic field in three layers model of air, seawater and seabed, the distributing characteristics of underwater coupling static magnetic and high altitude coupling static magnetic field are analyzed. Combined with the detection level of underwater and aviation, the detection feasibility based on the corruption related magnetic field is analyzed. By comparing with static magnetic field caused by magnetic materials, it is pointed out that when degaussing technology reaches a certain level, the corruption related magnetic field may become the main impact factor of magnetic field detection.

articleTitle: Suppression of vortex induced vibration of a circular cylinder by four control rods
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The suppression of vortex induced vibration (VIV) of a circular cylinder by four small control rods at a Reynolds number of 5000 is studied by two-dimensional numerical simulations. The main purpose of this study is to investigate the effects of the vortex shedding of the control rods on the VIV suppression. The four rods are in an axially square arrangement surrounding the cylinder. The rod-to-cylinder diameter ratio is 0.2 and the gap between the rod and the cylinder is the same as the diameter of the rods. A lock-in regime still exists when there are four rods surrounding the cylinder but the maximum vibration amplitude in the lock-in regime is only 19% of that of a bare cylinder without rods. Outside the lock-in regime the vibration has two frequencies, and they are the vortex shedding frequencies of the cylinder and rod, respectively. The vortex shedding from the two upstream rods suppresses the VIV by breaking the coherence of the shear layers from above and below the cylinders. The mechanism of the VIV suppression by the two downstream rods is that the flow through the two downstream cylinder-to-rod gaps attach to the back surface of the cylinder, resulting in a weakening of the vortex shedding from the cylinder.

articleTitle: Review of submarine cable design lifetime
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Summarizes the current research status of submarine cable lifetime from three aspects: insulation lifetime, fatigue lifetime and armor corrosion. Aiming at the research of submarine cable insulation lifetime, the electrical, thermal and combined electro-thermal stress insulation lifetime models are summarized, and the impact of temperature gradient effect and space charge on the aging lifetime of insulating materials under the action of DC electric field is examined. These two topics-the corrosion behavior of metal armor in a maritime environment and the fatigue lifetime modeling approach of submarine cables-are summed together. Finally, based on the information in this study, a brief discussion of the research's existing limitations is made, and the paper evaluates the direction that submarine cable lifetime research will take in the future.

articleTitle: Research on the influence of misalignment arrangement on the interference characteristics of double row wingsail in sail-assisted ships
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: In order to study the interference characteristics between multiple wingsails of sail-assisted vessels during navigation, the Reynolds averaged N-S equation is used to numerically simulate wingsails performance under steady operating conditions. The results indicate that in the double row ar-rangement scheme, the wake of upstream wingsail interferes with the flow field of downstream wingsail, causing the downstream wingsail stall. Through the lateral misalignment arrangement of the downstream wingsail and the upstream wingsail, an arrangement scheme with good propulsion performance was obtained. In the scheme where the downstream and upstream wingsails are horizontally misaligned by 2.4c, the wake of upstream wingsail has the smallest interference effect on the downstream wingsail, and the comprehensive propulsion performance is the best with the relative wind direction angle of 90°, the lateral spacing of 4c, and the longitudinal spacing of 10c.

articleTitle: Modeling and experimental research of cable-drive anti-swing device for shipboard crane
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The marine environment is complex and changeable. Therefore, the shipboard crane will be greatly disturbed during operations. In order to solve the swing problem of the shipboard payload, improving the working efficiency and operating safety, a cable-drive anti-swing device (CDASD) based on mechanical limiting-location is proposed. Four steel cables are used to limit the spatial position of the constant tension hook. Simultaneously, the payload swing can be eliminated rapidly with the four driving cables. The CDASD for the shipboard crane is simplified as a constrained pendulum with a motorial base, and its three-dimensional mathematical model are established by damping theory and Lagrange method. Then, the length and tension value of the driving cable are analysed, investigating the effect law on the payload swing. Finally, simulative and experimental results are provided to verify the effectiveness and security of the cable-drive anti-swing device for shipboard crane on a self-built experiment platform.

articleTitle: Passive ranging of synthetic aperture beamforming based on fringe
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: In this paper, a method of synthetic aperture beamforming based on fringe is proposed, which can locate the sound source by using only a single hydrophone. First, considering the Doppler effect between a single hydrophone and a moving sound source, the weaping operator is used to eliminate the Doppler frequency shift. The conventional and fringe based synthetic aperture beamforming methods are used to process the sound signal, and the radial velocity of the sound source is estimated. According to the deviation range of the two radial velocity estimates and the slope of the interference fringe of the LOFAR diagram, the waveguide invariant and the horizontal distance of the sound source are finally determin-ed. The feasibility of passive ranging with a single hydrophone was verified by SwellEx-96 experiment.

articleTitle: Bearing performance of suction anchor for floating offshore wind turbines
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The suction anchor serves as a floating wind turbine base, enduring inclined loads in all directions. Its loadbearing varies from the double angle sum system, allowing optimization of the cross-point location for ample suction power. This study focuses on the semi-floating platform's three-anchor combined suction anchor foundation. Utilizing five incline degrees and six mooring points, numerical simulations explore the foundation's response to different loads. Load impact reveals the foundation's bearing performance relies on mooring point position, uncovering optimal locations. Findings highlight superior ultimate bearing capacity under 15° and 30° loading for a single tension anchor compared to 45°, 60°, and 75°. Upon load application, anchor-side soil fails translation, forming continuous plastic failure on the front side. Soil pressure at anchor's front and rear increases linearly with depth; lower angle correlates with higher ground pressure. Symmetrical along mooring cable, max pressure occurs at 0° and min at 180° behind the anchor.

articleTitle: Research on transient response characteristics of ship multi-engine propulsion shafting under ice load impact
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: To study the dynamic response characteristics of propulsion shafting in ship multi-engine power plant in ice area, as well as to assess the operational reliability of the plant under the impact of ice load. The time-varying characteristics of gears are introduced into the torsional vibration model of the multi- engine propulsion shafting, and the system rotational speed drop generated by the sudden impact of ice load is considered. Finally, solving the dynamic response of the main components of the system in the double-engine mode and single-engine mode based on the step-by-step integration method. The results show: among the four ice loads, Case2 causes the most obvious dynamic response to the shafting. In both propulsion modes, the double-engine propulsion mode produces a greater response than the single-engine propulsion mode. In the double-engine propulsion mode, the time-varying meshing force of the pinion on the engaging side is slightly bigger than the pinion gear on the running side. The improved model proposed in the paper can be used for transient calculation of sudden ice load on a ship multi-engine power plant propulsion system, which can provide reference for the safety assessment of ship in ice area.

articleTitle: Bistatic scattering of acoustic waves by an underwater elastic cylinder
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: On the basis of the normal series solution of an infinite cylinder and the approximate solution of a finite cylinder provided by previous scholars, the partial wave shape functions of each order of an elastic cylinder are obtained using the method of partial wave resonance, and the related resonance frequencies are determined. Based on the Regge trajectory method, the phase velocity dispersion curve of the elastic cylinder is also established. Spectral analysis of plane wave scattering from an elastic cylinder at different received angles is conducted. The results reveal that the peaks of the partial wave resonance curve correspond one-to-one with the peaks of the pure elastic scattering shape function, and the frequency widths of different types of wave resonance vary under the same order. The trajectory model, calculated according to the phase difference, can approximately represent the near-side Rayleigh interference, as well as the near-side and far-side Rayleigh wave interference of the specular mode. The research results may provide useful for identifying underwater complex structural targets based on elastic wave characteristics.

articleTitle: Enhancing vessel stability through hull design
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Maritime transport safety is and will always be a concern, as history has proven how disastrous and costly maritime accidents can be. Vessel capsizing and sinking due to damage stability remain an issue that cannot be totally remedied. A design is proposed where two cylindrical-shape with a closed paraboloid or cone-shape front end, one cylinder is smaller than the other, and on the inner wall of the bigger cylinder is connected with round rails containing lubricated bearings to minimise friction. The smaller cylinder into which cargo is loaded is then fitted inside the bigger one such that it freely slides in the larger vessel, allowing it to re-establish its centre of gravity if it becomes out of balance. A mathematical and ANSYS (Hydrodynamic Diffraction and Rigid Dynamics) analysis demonstrates a 360 degree of stability when confronted by external force, as this cylindrical design doesn't capsize. Whenever the outer cylinder turns or slides on water, the inner cylinder simply self-slides within to adapt and restore the centre of gravity. Furthermore, rotation can be self-initiated to change damage part submersed in water where leakage is coming from, to the Vessel's upper part out of water, hence stopping leakage and Vessel's flooding.

articleTitle: Numerical and experimental analysis of surface divergence by Fr of submerged vehicle
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Surface wake divergence field that excited by submerged vehicle is important hydrodynamic physics field and source of non-acoustic detection. In this paper, the numerical and experimental analysis are used to obtain the free surface divergence field in a stratified ocean. The PIV experiments are used to verify the results of numerical analysis results in a stratified pool. The researches results show that divergence characteristics of simulation and experiment are approximately, for example the angle and intensity of divergence. With the increase of the Froude number, the divergence angles on the free surface gradually decrease from double e-index function to linear function. The divergence intensity of surface wakes was increased and then decreased. The change rules of intensity that excited by the submarine models were maintained consistent with experimental results of the pool with scaling model.

articleTitle: Marine hybrid SOFC-GT system with contact-type gas turbine and over-expansion
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The paper focuses on enhancing the efficiency of marine hybrid systems for generating electrical and thermal energy. These systems consist of solid oxide fuel cells and a gas turbine with over-expansion. Unlike prior studies, the research establishes the potential benefits of employing a gas turbine cycle with steam injection into the combustor and an over-expansion turbine for efficiently utilizing the exhaust gases from fuel cells. This approach not only enhances the overall efficiency of the power system but also differs significantly from earlier investigations. The versatility of marine power plants, operating in multiple modes, underscores the considerable potential of integrating solid oxide fuel cells and a gas turbine to optimize the efficiency of ship operations. A design framework for a marine power plant incorporating solid oxide fuel cells and a gas turbine with over-expansion has been devised. Thorough thermal calculations for such a system have been conducted, yielding scientifically grounded insights for the development of promising energy systems combining fuel cells and gas turbines. This contributes to a deeper understanding of energy conversion processes in such systems, paving the way for the creation of highly efficient, decarbonized energy systems tailored for marine applications.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of LNG precooling process in fuel tanks for marine applications
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: With the proposal of carbon neutrality/carbon peaking strategy, Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG), as a representative of clean energy, has attracted wide attention from all walks of life. This paper takes the Mark III fuel tank of an LNG container ship as the object, and analyzes the pre-cooling rule of the single-side spray mode LNG. A discrete phase model is used to simulate LNG spray and gasification, a component transport model is used to simulate gas exchange diffusion, and a UDF that conforms to the LNG real-time control spray logic in the precooling process is loaded to simulate and analyze the high-frequency linear predictive cooling effect and adjust the impact of real-time adjustment of LNG spray rate on the flow field change, precooling effect, pre-cooling time and precooling cost. Compared with the results of the fuel tank gas test, the deviation of the numerical model simulation results is less than 5%. At the same cooling rate, different control intervals have a more obvious effect on the temperature change of the fuel tank, and different control intervals show similar LNG spray rate rules. The research results of this paper provide parameters and suggestions for the optimization and improvement of LNG fuel tank precooling monitoring and control system.

articleTitle: Prediction of wave run-up on single cylinder based on LSTM neural network
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: As the column cylinder is commonly used for floating structures and the sea state is random, the wave run-up on cylinder with ocean waves interaction is always with strong nonlinearity and randomness. Compared to neural network technology, the traditional CFD calculation method is not a suitable way for the prediction. In this paper, STAR-CCM+ is used to establish a numerical wave tank to generate of 300s irregular wave data, and the monitoring points are arranged around the single cylinder to capture the wave height. Through dimensionless processing and comparison, the time-history wave height data on the monitoring point with the largest wave run-up is selected as the data source. The long short-term memory neural network model is used for training and prediction, and the accuracy of the results are analyzed. It provides a practical guidance scheme for accurate prediction of wave run-up.

articleTitle: Exploration for improving shear mechanisms of graphene oxide on epoxy coatings from atomistic insights
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The shear performance of epoxy (EP) coating modified by graphene nanosheet (GNS) and graphene oxide (GO) was evaluated by molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to explore the improved shear mechanism from an atomic view. A typical shear structure composed of epoxy coatings and bi-level copper layer was built according to the standard shear pattern. Obvious shear deformation was observed for the pure epoxy, while the deformation resistance was improved after filling GO due to stronger hydrogen bond adsorption effect. The improvement mechanism was analysed by extracting interfacial energy. This study is helpful for discovering shear failure mechanism and high performance coating design.

articleTitle: A study on load identification technology of multi-support bearing based on pedestal response
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: To identify the bearing load in a complicated and multi-supported rotor-bearing system, this paper takes a method which combines simulation transfer function and bearing-base response test. Meanwhile the singular value decomposition method was used to solve the inverse problem. And the load identification model was validated by plate testing. To solve the pathological problem of the frequency response function matrix, this paper proposed a D-optimal design coupled sequence exchange method to optimize the measurement points. The results show that the technique used in this paper can successfully and accurately identify the bearing load, which can be adopted in engineering application. The D-optimal design coupled sequence exchange method can greatly improve the bearing load identification accuracy by reducing the condition number of the transfer matrix. The load identification accuracy does not im-prove with increasing the number of measurement points, and the additional measurement points will increase the load identification error.

articleTitle: Research on an adaptive-damping-control strategy of wave energy converter by AMESIM/STARCCM+ co-simulation
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Wave energy is a potential renewable source in the world. Wave energy converters (WEC) have been designed for converting wave energy to electricity. To realize the engineering application and commercial value of WECs, researchers and engineers aim to get higher efficiency of WECs. This study provides a novel adaptive and variable damping control strategy, which can achieve a fast and real-time matching of the optimal damping in the real sea states. First-order linear waves were established in AMESIM to study power-generation performance under different wave conditions. Hydrodynamic analysis was investigated in STARCCM+, and the convergence studies with respect to the meshes size and time step at the same time. Finally, the results in AMESIM are in sufficient agreement with the results in STARCCM+, which verified the reliability of the analytical process.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of heavy oil heating in wreck tanks
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Study the thermal diffusion of the heavy oil in the fuel oil compartment under the two conditions of heating rod and hot oil injection for the heavy oil in the fuel oil compartment of a given size, and analyse the average thermal diffusion and spatial distribution of the temperature of the heavy oil in the fuel oil compartment. Base on the numerical analysis results, it can be concluded that using a heating rod to heat the heavy oil in the fuel oil compartment results in a significant increase in temperature over time before reaching a stable temperature. When injecting hot oil, the heavy oil temperature in the fuel oil compartment increases faster over time than the temperature increase rate of the heating rod. The higher temperature of the injected hot oil, the higher heavy oil temperature in the fuel oil compartment. Compared with heating the heavy oil with a heating rod, the use of injecting hot oil has a significant advantage in increasing the temperature of the oil and the speed of its movement. The numerical analysis results can provide reference for the arrangement of heating rods for the heavy oil recovery of wrecks. The simulation of hot oil injection can solve the problem of slow flow of heavy oil in the fuel oil compartment and difficulty in extracting heavy oil at the oil extraction port.

articleTitle: Experimental study on the effect of impact point spacing on the penetration resistance of fiber reinforced laminated target plate
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: In order to investigate the performance of the target plate's resistance to secondary penetration at different spacing of impact points, this paper uses a first stage light gas gun device to conduct secondary penetration experiments on three types of laminated target plates at two different spacing. From the aspects of target plate energy absorption and specific energy absorption, the influence of the distance between the two impact points on the anti penetration performance of the composite target plate is analyzed. The results show that the damage caused by the first penetration will to some extent affect the energy absorption effect of the second penetration, and the energy absorption defense effect is weaker at positions closer to the damage than at positions farther away; under the same spacing between impact points, the structure of "aluminum alloy plate+2mm thick UD cloth laminated plate+three-dimensional fabric composite plate+aluminum alloy plate" has the best resistance to secondary penetration due to its higher proportion of fiber materials and higher lateral stress wave transmission effect.

articleTitle: Research on monitoring and predictive analysis of reclamation settlement
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Reclamation projects often involve large-scale engineering. Taking a certain land reclamation project in Shanghai as an example, where the fill material primarily comes from dredged soil from waterways, significant variations exist in soil characteristics among different sections of the waterway and between wet and dry seasons. In order to effectively control the fill elevation and smoothness within the reclaimed area, accurate predictive analysis of the settlement observation results of the fill material is required. Based on the observed settlement curve, it was found that the settlement of the fill material primarily occurs within the initial 6 months, and during this period, the settlement rate is notably high. Employing the three-point method, an effective predictive analysis was conducted on the observed settlement volume of the fill material. Research findings indicate that the predicted results are consistently higher than the actual observed results, with differences typically falling within the range of 30 mm. The predictive outcomes tend to be conservative. Additionally, based on the predictive results, it is recommended to reserve at least a 30 mm surplus of fill material before commencing the reclamation.

articleTitle: Correlation analysis between the structure and unsaturated characteristic parameters of clay
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: In order to explore the relationship between soil structure and unsaturated strength characteristics, compression test and soil-water characteristic curve tests were carried out for structural clay of Zhanjiang Formation, and the structural damage coefficient of undisturbed soil, S, at different depths and the soil-water characteristic curves were obtained by tensimeter method. The parameters α, m and n in FX model were obtained by analyzing the soil-water characteristic curve. According to the analysis between FX model parameters and S, shown that there were strong correlation between them: The parameters α and m will decrease with the increasing of S, but n will increases. Which means the stronger the soil structure was, the stronger the water holding capacity was, the larger the residual water content was, and the smaller the dehydration rate was. Then their fitting functions on S have been obtained. The study results could provide some useful reference to establish the constitutive relationship of the unsaturated structural soil.

articleTitle: Study of vortex-induced vibration of cylinder with teeth at different attack angles
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Cylinder with teeth is a typical structural form of the leg chord of jack-up, In this paper, vortex-induced vibration(VIV) of an elastically supported cylinder with teeth at different attack angles was studied using the overset mesh technique, the mass ratio of the structure is 6.07, the attach angles are 0°, 45°, and 90°, and the reduced velocity (Ur) range is 3-30. An analysis was conducted on the motion trajectory, vibration modes, vortex shedding patterns. The results indicate that different attack angles have significant impact on vibration frequency, vortex shedding frequency. At 0° and 90° attach angles. VIV of cylinder with teeth is similar to cylinder. The vibration frequency and vortex frequency both increase with the increase of Ur. At 45° attach angle, low reduction velocity dominant vortex vibration and high reduced speed dominant galloping. In the attack angle range of 0°-90°, the motion trajectory and vibration response of cylinder with tooth are different from cylinder.

articleTitle: Fluid-solid coupling-based nonlinear central composite optimization design for ocean wharf station
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The entry of underwater submersibles into an ocean wharf station generates certain impact forces that result in vibrations, wear, and deformations in the ocean wharf station. To address this issue, a comprehensive structural design optimization was performed on the ocean wharf station's framework. A parameterized model was designed, and a simulated environment for fluid-structure interaction was set up to serve the simulation calculations of the central composite design algorithm. Response surface and regression analysis were used for multi-objective optimization of the simulation results, which led to determining the most suitable structural parameters and obtaining the nonlinear model design. The model generated through the algorithm achieved a 27% optimization in strain, 29% optimization in stress, and 42% optimization in deformation. The average accuracy of the nonlinear model reached 97%, demonstrating its effectiveness. Furthermore, the high accuracy of the nonlinear regression model and the highly linear distribution of sensitivity scatter plots further validates the accuracy of the simulation.

articleTitle: Optimization of the twisted rudder based on SBD technology
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: In recent years, with the international tension and the surge in energy consumption, how to make full use of energy has become an increasingly important issue, and the development of energy-saving technology of ships as shipping tools has attracted much attention from all sectors of society. Energy-saving appendages have been widely used in ships because of their advantages of low cost and simple installation. The twisted rudder is a new type of energy-saving appendage that can better adapt to the propeller race and improve the propeller propulsion efficiency. Previous twisted rudder optimization results depend on the designer's experience and often take a lot of time. In this paper, a more advanced SBD method is adopted to optimize a conventional rudder. SBD technology combines FFD technology, optimization algorithm and CFD technology. In the optimization process, the propeller and rudder are analyzed as an overall system, and the overall optimization efficiency is selected as an optimization goal.

articleTitle: Study and application on calculation model of uniaxial compressive strength in harbor coastal strata
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: It is common for foundation piles to be embedded into bedrock through overburden in port coastal engineering, and it is particularly critical to explore the bearing layer that can meet the bearing capacity of marine engineering buildings. The uniaxial compressive strength of rock is closely related to the bearing capacity, and its measurement is greatly affected by the state of rock core. Severely damaged or irregularly shaped cores can result in loss of local formation data. The current study develops a calculation model to investigate the relationship between uniaxial compressive strength and other easy-to-obtain physical parameters of core, based on rough sets and multiple linear methods. Comparison between modeling and experimental results shows a satisfactory agreement. The successful application of this calculation model in regional 3D modeling of a port building design demonstrates its feasibility.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of precooling for the fuel tank of LNG-powered ship
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Taking the fuel tank of a LNG-power bulk carrier as the research object, a numerical model of heat transfer analysis was established using CFD software to study the precooling of LNG bunker. The precooling operation mainly spray the nitro-gen and liquid nitrogen in different stages. Using the computational fluid dynamics simulation method, the temperature characteristics of target zone were obtained through calculating and analyzing the nitrogen and liquid nitrogen spray process. The temperature drops and flow field characteristics of the bunker during the precooling process were mastered. It is shown that the temperature drop in the bunker during the precooling stage was related to the spray speed. When the spray speed of (liquid) nitrogen is faster, the faster the temperature decreased in the bunker.

articleTitle: Analysis of shock resistance and vibration isolation performance of a dual-layer vibration isolation device
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: In order to mitigate the impact of fan structural noise and vibration on ships, en-hance the survival capability of fan equipment under impact loads, and analyze the impact resistance and vibration isolation performance of the designed dual-layer isolation device. By utilizing the finite element method and referring to the BV043/85 standard, a time-domain simulation analysis was conducted to evaluate the impact resistance, stability, and vibration isolation performance of this dual-layer isolation system. The analysis results indicate that the anti-impact and vibra-tion isolation performance of the double-layer vibration isolation system in this structure meets the design requirements.

articleTitle: Study on the effect of the sailing performance of two ships in tandem
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Reasonable ship navigation information can effectively compensate for the tasks that cannot be accomplished by a single ship in highly dynamic waters, improve navigation performance and enhance ship maneuverability. Based on the N-S equation and VOF theory, this paper uses Starccm+ software to simulate and analyze the sailing performance of serial ships, discusses the sailing characteristics of two ships working together in waves. The results show that tandem sailing can improve the sailing performance and achieve the purpose of drag reduction.

articleTitle: Hydrodynamics of a wind-wave-solar hybrid floating platform
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The wind, wave and solar power resources are wealth and widely distributed within the deep ocean areas, attracting increasing interest all over the world. The feasibility of combined exploration of these resources is explored in this work by proposing a wind-wave-solar hybrid floating platform. A barge-type floating offshore wind turbine (FOWT) foundation is selected for the integrations of solar photovoltaic panels, and four cross-symmetric distributed oscillating water column (OWC) devices are mounted inside the foundation. Hydrodynamics of this hybrid system is investigated using Computational Fluid Dynamics simulations with the software Star-CCM+. The model solves Navier - Stokes equations and utilizes the Volume of Fluid (VOF) technique for capturing free surface motions. Comparisons with experimental measurements collected for a submersible platform integrating FOWT and OWC technologies are carried for validating the numerical model established. It is found that the piston-type resonance inside the four OWC chambers occurs at the same wave frequency, leading to the largest wave energy capturing, and the OWC arranged on the rear side performs the best in shorter waves. Correspondingly, local peaks in platform motions and the mooring tensions are observed at this wave frequency due to large resonant water motion inside the OWC chambers.

articleTitle: Acoustic performance and bandgap characteristics of a duct array with integrated reactive silencers
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: In this paper, the noise attenuation performance of periodical arranged integrate silencers involving quarter wavelength tubes and Herschel-Quincke(H-Q) tubes and expansion chambers has been investigated. The effect of geometric parameters on sound transmission loss of individual reactive-interfere silencer has been examined. Then, band structure analysis has been conducted for the models of integrated silencer with infinite periods. It is found that coupling of local resonance and Bragg reflection can be achieved by adjusting the geometric parameter of the silencer array.

articleTitle: A small scale wave energy converter development by experimental test
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Waves contain huge energy, and very little wave energy may meet a small-scale ocean instrument demand. In this paper, an inner pendulum float wave energy converter is developed. The buoy is designed and its energy capture test is conducted in a wide wave flume in Ningbo University. The buoy has an elliptic top section with long axis often along wave direction, the bottom is semicircle in the vertical section along wave direction. The inner pendulum moving in wave direction is installed whose axle driving a three-phase AC motor to generate electricity. The electric circuit is designed to rectify AC to DC and to store DC electricity into a battery. Electric resistances are set as operating load, value of resistances and voltage on a resistance are measured to calculate the power captured by the device. The test is conducted in regular wave, the relationship between power captured and wave condition are analyzed. The system captures more energy at wave period 1.0s. It is predicted that when the system adopted on ocean fishing field, the averaged power is about 279 mW, and the maximum power is about 1306 mW.

articleTitle: Comprehensive analysis of conceptual propulsion systems for autonomous merchant ships from a seafarer's perspective
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: With the great potential benefit in economics/safety/eco-friendliness recognized in the conception of autonomous merchant shipping, several funded research projects on the development the conception has been initiated by International Maritime Organization and some shipping research entities. Several technical frameworks and conceptions for unmanned navigation are proposed. However few detailed discussion can be found on conceptual design of propulsion plant. Hence, this paper present a feasibility discussion on propulsion plant for a unmanned merchant shipping especially from a seaman perspective, and hopes to outline a picture of conceptual engine room for coming autonomous merchant shipping.

articleTitle: Reliability calculation method of ship distributed degaussing system considering with power module backup and winding reconstruction
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: With the large size of modern ships and the increasing requirements of naval demagnetization technology, the demagnetization system develops to distributed type, and the system reliability can be improved by modular demagnetization power supply module redundancy backup and demagnetization winding reconfiguration design in the distributed demagnetization system. In order to calculate the reliability of the distributed demagnetization system, the typical design principles of modular demagnetization power module backup and demagnetization winding reconfiguration are analyzed, and the design schemes such as 1+1 backup or N<sub>m</sub>+1 backup for the demagnetization power supply, overall N-1 reconfiguration for the longitudinal winding, no reconfiguration for the single-layer transverse winding or vertical winding, and local N-1 reconfiguration for the double-layer transverse winding or vertical winding are determined. Based on the basic reliability model and the above design principles, the reliability calculation model and method applicable to the distributed demagnetization system are established, and the reliability enhancement capability of the demagnetization system is analyzed and calculated as an example, and the calculation method can be used to guide the reliability design of the demagnetization system.

articleTitle: Experimental study on vibration damping property of cruise chimney wall structure
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: In order to study the influence of different damping on cruise ship chimney en-closure structural vibration, modal test and transfer function test were carried out by laying large-scale steel plates. The vibration reduction characteristics of three types of damping, namely water-based damping coating, blended constrained damping coating and constrained damping patch, were analyzed. The influence of damping material and its thickness on vibration reduction was analyzed by using average transfer function and vibration attenuation rate per unit weight as evalua-tion indexes. The results show that in the thin plate structure, the damping thick-ness has a great influence on the loss factor, and the water-based damping loss factor with smaller thickness is slightly smaller.
