The damping patch has no con-struction thickness error and the vibration reduction effect is the best The vibra-tion reduction effect reaches best when the damping patch has no construction thickness error, but the water-based damping construction is simple, suitable for complex shape components and the vibration attenuation rate per unit weight is greater. In the application of thick plate, the water-based damping coating with the same thickness can also achieve the vibration reduction effect of blending con-strained damping. The experimental results can provide a more accurate reference for the selection of damping materials for engineering applications.

articleTitle: Interactions between wave groups in bimodal sea states
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Interactions between wave groups are dominant generation mechanisms of extreme waves. It was clearly explained in bimodal sea state with fixed intermodal distance, without considering the influence of wave configurations. The variation of interactions between wave groups is to be investigated, based on a two-dimensional numerical wave tank using High-order Spectral method. Results show that the intermodal distance and the sea-swell energy ratio have little effect on the frequency spectra of second-order harmonics, but as the intermodal distance becomes larger, the higher-order harmonics generated by cross interactions become less, quite similar but more sensitive to the energy distribution.

articleTitle: Numerical study on equilibrium beach profiles
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Investigating equilibrium beach profiles has attracted the attention of scientists and engineers since a long time ago. In this study, sand transport patterns induced by undertow, wave nonlinearity, and bed slope and features of equilibrium beach profiles generated by these sand transport patterns are provided using a simple time-averaged numerical model. The model results show that rollers play an important role in the features of equilibrium profiles. Rollers make the offshore sand transport related to undertow larger than onshore sand transport at the region shoreward of the wave breaking point, and this benefits to sandbar formation. Sandbar is not found if the contribution of rollers on undertow and thus on the corresponding offshore sand transport is excluded. Also, the relation between wave parameters and equilibrium beach profiles is discussed. Three kinds of equilibrium beach profiles are found: berm, single sandbar, and multi-sandbar profiles. With the incident wave height increasing or wave period decreasing, the equilibrium beach profiles are transformed from a berm profile to a single sandbar profile and then to a multi-sandbar profile, this being consistent with the equilibrium profile type based on the relative fall velocity developed by Dean (1973).

articleTitle: Numerical simulation and experimental research of cavitation water jet impacting titanium metal
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: In order to explore the surface modification mechanism of cavitation water jet on titanium metal, this paper combined the characteristics of organ pipe nozzle and self-excited oscillation nozzle to design a composite nozzle. By combining numerical simulation with experimental research, the cavitation water jet flow field generated by composite nozzles is simulated numerically by different inlet pressure and cavitation target distance, and the submerged cavitation water jet is verified experimentally. The results show that cavitation water jet treatment significantly improves the surface properties of titanium. Inlet pressure, cavitation target distance and cavitation impact time have great influence on the surface modification of titanium metal. The best inlet pressure is 25MPa, the best cavitation target distance is 20mm, and the best cavitation impact time is 20min. With the increase of cavitation impact time, the surface wettability of titanium metal increases first and then decreases, and the surface microhardness increases first and then decreases.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of two-dimensional periodic focusing wave
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Focused waves are generally considered to be effective simulations of freak waves or extreme sea conditions observed in the ocean for marine structures design. The understanding of factors in generating prescribed focusing wave is of great importance for its generation in both numerical and physical wave tank. In this paper, based on Fluent dynamic mesh technique, a simulate method is proposed for generating multiple focused waves within a relatively short time. This can improve the efficiency of the hydrodynamic testing of coastal and offshore structures. In this study, the variation of interactions between wave groups is to be investigated by changing the input predefined period, it was found that the focused wave crest increases with the decrease of the predefined period, and the actual focal location is somehow shifted behind the theoretical value, the iterative method is used to correct the deviation of the focused position caused by nonlinearity with the wave propagation. The results show that this method can generate periodic focusing waves with different predefined periods. The time interval between wave groups has great effect on the simulation of PFW. As the pre-set period decreases, the interval between two neighbouring focusing wave group become less or even overlapping in the PFW, and the nonlinear influence between waves increases, which is not conducive to generate PFW target profile, it is not easy to generate periodic focusing waves, and the required number of iterations increases.

articleTitle: Removal of anti-corrosion coatings from advanced marine composite surfaces
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Currently, composite materials are widely used throughout the marine industry, and yet their sus-ceptibility to corrosion remains an unsolved problem. In order to avoid corrosion caused by highly corrosive seawater, temperature, salinity and biological pollu-tion of advanced marine vessels, which are mainly made of fiber composites, an-ticorrosion coatings are widely used on advanced vessels. However, the anti-corrosion coating on the surface of composites can fall off prematurely due to high-speed rotation, friction with seawater, etc. In order to ensure the proper functioning of the anti-corrosion coating, it is necessary to remove the damaged coating and re-coated it. In order to address this issue, this study proposes for the first time the use of plastic abrasive air-jet machining to remove the damaged coating with-out damaging the fibers. The particle velocity of plastic abrasive was analyzed by modeling, the maximum particle velocity at the nozzle exit was obtained, and the impact stress probability distribution of the particle erosion the workpiece was investigated. The landscape's morphology of the eroded surface was observed through Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) and the coating removal mechanism was analyzed. Finally, the coating removal rate under different process conditions was investigated. The theoretical reference is provided for the nondestructive substrate removal of anti-corrosive coatings on advanced marine surfaces.

articleTitle: Design and dynamic characteristics of the interconnected suspension system for small rescue crafts
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Traditional small rescue crafts are mainly equipped with a spring-damper suspension system, which has poor damping ability to wave and is not conducive to human life rescue under bad sea conditions. To solve this problem, a novel hydraulic interconnected suspension system with good stiffness and damping characteristics is proposed to reduce the impact of waves on the rescue ship body. Based on the synchronous interconnection of double-acting hydraulic cylinders, the circuit adopts a special intermediate hydraulic cylinder as an indirect pressure transmission device. Without affecting its ride comfort, the design enables the small rescue craft to improve its adaptability to waves. Employing the motion compensation mechanism, this paper explores the working process of the rescue craft and makes an integrated design for the suspension system, thus realizing the coordinated control of 3-DOF position compensation. The simulation model of the suspension system is established and the dynamic characteristics of the suspension system under different sea conditions are obtained through multi-sea state simulation. Results reveal that the new suspension system can effectively alleviate the vibration of the hull under the sea condition of Level 4. The vibration amplitude of the hull is about 30% of the buoy.

articleTitle: Turbulent viscosity effect on irregular wave simulation accuracy
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The effect on the simulation accuracy is studied by comparing the traditional turbulence viscosity formula and the improved turbulence viscosity formula on the simulation of different sea states, including errors in significant wave height and average period, the changes in turbulent viscosity and consistency with theoretical spectra.Wave-making boundaries and wave-making sources generate irregular waves.A wave-dissipation momentum source is also used to make the waves at the end of the flume disappear. In addition, in order to suppress the overgrowth of turbulent viscosity in the tank, an improved turbulent viscosity formula was adopted.For the results of different sea states, the maximum error of the wave characteristic parameters (significant wave height H1/3 and average wave period T0) reach to 33% and 15% with the traditional turbulent viscosity formula. Using the modified turbulent viscosity formula, these errors can be reduced to 30% and 12%, respectively.This study proves that the modified turbulent viscosity formula can stabilize the turbulent viscosity within a reasonable range in the numerical flume and guarantee the irregular wave simulation accuracy.

articleTitle: The research of submarine pipeline's collision impacted by anchor of shipsin neritic zone
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: In neritic zone with dense shipping, ship anchoring operations pose a potential threat of damage to submarine pipelines. The paper is based on the energy analysis method to analyze the impact damage of ship anchoring on submarine pipelines in neritic zone. By establishing a mathematical model for the impact damage of submarine pipeline anchoring operations, the degree of damage such as anchoring impact and depression depth of submarine pipelines under different burial layer thicknesses and concrete thicknesses is studied, and a safety zone for the burial depth of submarine pipelines in shallow water areas is proposed.It provides a method and basis for the construction of submarine pipelines in neritic zone of China.

articleTitle: Ship structure-borne noise analysis based on secondary development of VA one
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: An efficient method is presented for the prediction of the ship structure-borne noise. Statistical Energy Analysis (SEA) is used, and the equations used for the SEA parameters are also presented. Traditionally, the SEA method requires a great deal of work after structures are modelled. It is almost laborious and time-consuming to set damping loss factors and excitation loads for large structures such as ships. In the presented method, the secondary development of VA One is applied, and the processing programs are used in the context of Matlab. Through the secondary development, setting of damping loss factor and loading, solving of SEA model have been carried out. The effectiveness of the present method is illustrated by the computer run of the box model, which containing 16 plate subsystems and 3 acoustic cavity subsystems. The effects of damping loss factors are discussed.

articleTitle: Analysis of wave absorbing effect of numerical wave tank
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Numerical wave tanks have a wide range of applications in marine and offshore engineering, such as: hydrodynamic modeling and simulation of ships and marine structures in the marine environment. Vibration and noise analysis of ships and marine structures. Motion control research of ships and marine structures. As an important experimental device for simulating fluid motion, numerical water wave tank has been widely used in various fields. Wave generation and wave absorbing are two key techniques for numerical wave tank. Wave generation is usually achieved by exciting waves on the water surface, while wave absorbing is to absorb the generated waves by some measures. Wave generation is the first step of numerical wave tank simulation. This paper mainly introduces the research status of the wave absorbing effect of numerical wave tanks, and discusses the application of numerical wave tanks in wave absorbing. Through software simulation, different variables were compared to verify the effectiveness of the numerical wave tank wave suppression system. The significance of researching wave generation and wave absorbing in numerical wave tank lies in improving the simulation capability and practical application value of numerical wave tank. In addition, the continuous development of wave generation and wave absorbing contributes to some research fields. Therefore, the research and application of wave generation and wave absorbing in numerical wave tank have important theoretical and practical significance.

articleTitle: Study on equivalent method of statistical energy parameters of acoustic black hole plate based on the finite element method
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Acoustic black hole (ABH) is widely used in the field of structural vibration and noise reduction. When bent waves propagate into the ABH region, the propagation velocity of waves initially directed towards the centre of the ABH gradually decreases, while waves deviating from the ABH centre will deflect towards the centre. However, it has not yet been applied to acoustic calculation analysis in the high-frequency range within the framework of statistical analysis. This paper conducts simulation calculations of the sound insulation performance of ABH based on the finite element method (FEM) and equivalently translates the calculation results into the corresponding parameters required for statistical energy calculations. The ABH was designed on a uniform plate, and the wideband response of ABH is obtained through FEM, exploring optimal noise reduction strategies for ABH. The FEM results are equivalent to the parameters of the statistical energy analysis (SEA) and are assigned to the flat plate sub-systems. Finally, the sound insulation calculation of ABH in high frequency is realized based on SEA.

articleTitle: Design method for warship flight deck structures subjected to high temperature and wheel loads
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The flight deck is subjected to a combination of high temperatures and wheel impact loads during the landing of a Vertical Take-off and Landing (VTOL) aircraft. This paper analyses the structural response of deck plates and secondary members under the combined effect of high temperature and wheel pressure loads. Based on the temperature field distribution, the stresses of deck plates and secondary members at high temperatures are obtained theoretically, and the structural design method of the flight deck under the combined effect of high temperatures and wheel loads are proposed. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed design method, numerical analysis is carried out. The conclusions show that the results obtained from the design method agrees reasonably with the finite element simulations.

articleTitle: The positioning method of spherical inner detector for pipelines based on vibration signal
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The existing methods for locating pipeline inner detectors are commonly suitable for locate Pipeline Inspection Gauge. Aiming at the positioning requirements of the spherical inner detector in the subsea pipeline, a innovative method for positioning the spherical inner detector using the vibration caused when it passes over the girth weld is proposed. The basic principle of the positioning method and the reasons for the acceleration of the spherical inner detector passing over the girth weld are analysed. Using ADAMS to simulate the process of the spherical inner detector passes over the girth weld, the acceleration curve of the spherical inner detector was obtained, and the variation of the acceleration of the spherical inner detector was studied when the running speed and the height of the girth weld were changed. The results show that with the increase of the running speed and the height of the girth weld, the more intense the vibration caused by the girth weld, and the more obvious the variation of acceleration. The experiment of the spherical inner detector passing over the girth weld is carried out, and the variation of the acceleration obviously when passing over the girth weld.

articleTitle: Research on modeling method of radiated noise of underwater vehicle and its propagation characteristics under ice
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The simulation of radiated noise from underwater vehicles and the signal propagation characteristics in underwater acoustic channels are two major hot topics in the field of underwater acoustics. In this paper, first simulates the continuous spectrum, line spectrum, and modulation spectrum of underwater vehicles through empirical formulas and the design of FIR filters, and obtains the radiated noise power spectrum. On this basis, combined with the Bellhop acoustic toolbox, configure ocean environment files to simulate radiated noise signals transmitted through ocean channels, and, the influence of ice surface on underwater sound propagation is considered. Results show that the introduction of an ice-water mixed model in the simulation leads to a considerable increase in sound propagation loss. By adding icebergs at different distances on the lower surface of the ice, the sound propagation path and loss are calculated. Meanwhile, the position of iceberg has obvious influence on the propagation of rays.

articleTitle: Submarine warning detection methods of unmanned surface vessel
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Considering submarine detection needs and the characteristics of unmanned surface vessel, three typical types of submarine detection equipment for unmanned surface vessel, namely sonar buoy, towed sonar, and dipping sonar are introduced, and the working principle of each equipment is analysed. Then we set two typical submarine warning detection scenes for unmanned surface vessel according to actual combat needs, that is, warning detection for important fixed facility at sea, and warning detection for maritime formation. Methods and steps for unmanned surface vessel performing typical submarine warning detection tasks with typical submarine detection equipment are studied, the contents include sonar and unmanned surface vessel deployment, sonar and unmanned surface vessel demand, route planning, monitoring position, step length of detection, action timing, and unmanned surface vessel speed.

articleTitle: Numerical study on the motion response of port dredging vessel under the effect of group piles
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: A new type of dredging vessel is developed for the dredging needs under the high pile quay, which has the characteristics of small size, flexible movement, high dredging output and high efficiency. The piles underneath the quay have a large influence on the waves, which in turn has a non-negligible influence on the vessel movement, while the space underneath the quay is narrow, the piles cannot bear the lateral load, and the vessel itself carries a large amount of dredging operation equipment, so the adaptability of the dredging vessel is extremely demanding. In this paper, for this new type of vessel, the influence of group piles is considered, and the vessel motion response is analyzed in detail by numerical methods and compared with the calculation results without piles. The results show that the RAOs have some differences. Meanwhile, this paper selects typical working conditions and analyzes the vessel motion characteristics by time domain calculation, which provides important reference basis for the optimization of hull design, general arrangement, and the development of corresponding dredging technology and equipment.

articleTitle: Numerical study of the effect of natural convection on heat transfer in type B LNG cargo tank
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Type B LNG cargo tank is inevitably exposed to heat leakage from the external environment when it is transported at sea, and natural convection plays an important role in heat exchange between liquid and tank wall. In order to examine the temperature distribution of natural convection flow and heat transfer and investigate the processes of fluid flow in type B LNG cargo tanks. Numerical simulation research is conducted using the Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) approach, and a two-dimensional model is developed. In order to analyse how natural convection affects fluid flow and heat transmission, the Boussinesq equation is used to introduce the phenomenon. The findings demonstrate that the presence of natural convection in the LNG cargo tank increases the liquid velocity and chaotic eddy current, both of which significantly enhance the heat transfer among the liquid and the tank wall. The average temperature of LNG is significantly higher than that without natural convection, and more BOG is generated in the LNG cargo tank. The conclusions in this paper will be very helpful in the investigation of how natural convection affects the heat transmission of LNG cargo tanks during marine transportation.

articleTitle: Design and aerodynamic characteristics of groove type wing-in-ground-effect under wave action
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Because of its rapidity, concealment and versatility, the wing-in-ground-effect (WIG) ship has been developed rapidly, and the lifting capacity of WIG ship is becoming more and more important. As the main part to provide lift, the wing-in-ground-effect determines the load-carrying capacity of WIG ship. WIG configuration is a crucial parameter that affects the characteristic of WIG ship effect. In this study, the NACA0015 flat bottom WIG was taken as the parent WIG, and a new groove type WIG was designed. Based on the Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) method, the aerodynamic characteristics of the new type groove WIG were studied under different conditions include wave height and attack angles in wave effect. Compared with NACA0015 flat bottom WIG, the aerodynamic characteristics of the groove type WIG were obtained by studying its dynamic pressure distribution characteristics and surrounding characteristics of aerodynamic field. The results show that the groove type WIG has better lift characteristics under the wave conditions. The research results in this paper can be used to provide theoretical support for the design of WIG ship.

articleTitle: The hybrid model test of floating offshore wind turbine based on an aerodynamic actuation system
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The scaled model test is an important way to study the coupled dynamic performance of the floating offshore wind turbine (FOWT). Due to the scale effect, the dynamic characteristics of the scaled model are difficult to keep good similarity with that of the full-size model, which greatly weakens the significance of the model test. For this problem, an actuation system based on six fans was proposed in this paper. It could reproduce the six degrees of freedom (DOFs) aerodynamic loads generated by the wind turbine in the numerical model. The real-time communication between the software and hardware was built by a secondary compilation of the open-source code OpenFAST. The experimental results show that the designed actuation system can accurately track the target load signals and works as a low-pass filter. Based on a 1:50 scaled floating platform, the hybrid test model of a semi-submersible FOWT was constructed. Finally, several designed cases, including windwave misalignment, were carried out and the hydrodynamic characteristics of the FOWT were analyzed.

articleTitle: Experimental and numerical analysis on connecting-hole fishing ship's hydrodynamic performance
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Modified ship could provide an economic approach for fishing industry. Initially, two rows of holes were set under waterline to keep fluid connected and fish alive. The retained self-propelled ability of the ship could help fish adapt the variation of water temperature in different seasons. However, there lacks a reliable, mature, and unified standard for this ship form. In this paper, both experimental and numerical analysis were carried out on a modified bulk carrier to investigate its hydrodynamic performance. Potential theory and panel method were used in numerical analysis for its response under different wave states. Main detected data in model test include ship motion, vertical bending moment and shear force at key sections, sloshing pressure at key points, which would be compared with simulations. Several experimental techniques also were discussed in this paper. Result indicated that the hull model shows certain difference in response, even though under same floating state. Its response characteristic could be provided as reference for fishing and shipbuilding industry.

articleTitle: Effect of C/N ratio and sintering temperature on microstructure and mechanical properties of Ti (C, N)-based cermets
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: In this paper, the mechanical properties of Ti(C,N)-based cermets were further optimized by varying the C/N ratio and sintering temperature. The results show that all the cermets are consist of Co, TiB2, Ti(C, N), (Ti, W)(C,N) and CoW2B2 phases. A small amount of Co3C phase is present in the sintered specimens at 1600 and 1650°C. The Co3C phase disappears as the sintering temperature increases to 1700 °C. The decrease of C/N ratio and the increase of sintering temperature promote the densification of the cermets. The increase in C/N ratio enhances the mechanical properties of the cermets regardless of the sintering temperature. The hardness, bending strength and fracture toughness of the cermets show linear changes with increasing sintering temperature. The optimized comprehensive properties at a C/N ratio of 0.5 and a sintering temperature of 1650 °C are 1934 HV10, 855 MPa, and 7.07 MPa m1/2.

articleTitle: Study on the effects of siltation below the high pile wharf on the stress characteristics of pile foundation
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: China's coastal ports have 66% of silt coastal pile foundation berths, and long-term sediment back-siltation below the piled wharf leads to pile damage problems. In order to study the influence of sediment siltation height on the force characteristics of high-piled wharfs, this paper takes a certain high-piled wharf as a prototype, and selects its two typical sections to establish the finite element model of the fork pile wharf- slope soil and the fully straight pile wharf- slope soil. Additionally, the stress equilibrium method and the birth-death element method are employed to numerically simulate the original ground soil and the newly accumulated mud sediment. The results of numerical analysis show that: Sediment siltation under the wharf will cause the foundation soil to undergo horizontal displacement in the seaward direction and settlement dis-placement in the downward direction, and the displacement will be transferred to the pile foundation through the pile-soil interaction, thus affecting the force state of the wharf structure. For fork pile wharf structures, the top of the pile foundations on the shore side need to be attended to; for fully straight pile wharf structures, the seaward side of the top of the pile foundations and the underside of the beams need to be attended to. These areas are prone to tensile damage. These trends are also consistent with what happens in engineering practice.

articleTitle: Application of quantitative multi-attribute decision-making technology in offshore decommissioning
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: For years, offshore oil and gas resources have been extensively exploited across the globe. As a result, many facilities have reached the end of their useful lives and require decommissioning. However, the offshore industry has long been faced with the challenge of determining the best decommissioning methods, given the limitations imposed by regulations, technologies, costs, potential risks, and environmental impacts. This research aims to address this issue by developing a multi-attribute quantitative evaluation system called MADM-Q (Multi-attribute Decision Making-Quantitative). This system is designed to provide decision-makers with reliable quantitative evaluations during the engineering planning stage, allowing them to select the most suitable decommissioning options. By inputting only the basic information of the offshore facility and its location, the system can quickly generate a basic engineering cost range and the Individual Risk Per Annum (IRPA) value of the project. The system is composed of three modules: Engineering Cost Assessment System (ECAS), Hierarchical Analyst Domino Evaluation System (HADES), and Composite Impact Assessment System (CIAS). The methods employed in this system are rooted in physics and general-purpose industrial formulas. Furthermore, the system can be easily adapted for use in different regions of the world by adjusting commercial data based on the specific region.

articleTitle: Study on profile of embayed beach along coast in Zhejiang province
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The beaches in Zhejiang provincial coast belong to embayed beach, are constrained between the seawall (or bedrock) and the silty seabed. According to the survey of 12 typical beach profiles, the beach morphology generally presents a single slope shape, and the median diameter of grains in intertidal zone are basically similar. Comparing the linear model and Dean power function model, the linear model can better determine the beach profile. The slope of beach has a high linear correlation with the parameter combining wave parameters with median diameter. The formula of inverted slope ratio can be constructed by combined parameter, m=0.21H/(DT<sup>2</sup>)+8.1. The water depth at the foot of beach in mainland under averaged low tidal water level of spring is proportional to the wave height, in the weak wave areas where wave is shielded, the beach foot is higher than the low tidal level of spring tide, and in the open area where wave is strong, the beach foot is lower than the low tidal level. The water depth at the foot of the island beach is not significantly related to the wave height. The analysis of profile of coastal beaches can provide important references for beach restoration and the construction and design of beaches on mud flats.

articleTitle: Research on submarine search of unmanned surface vessel
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: We propose three typical submarine search loads for unmanned surface vessel, namely sonar buoy load, towed sonar load, and dipping sonar load based on submarine search task requirements and characteristics of unmanned surface vessel, and analyse the composition and working principle of each system. For each load, according to its composition and characteristics, submarine search workflow is designed. Then three typical submarine search scenes for unmanned surface vessel, namely patrol search, call search, and alert search are set according to actual combat needs. Submarine search plans for patrol search with dipping sonar, call search with sonar buoy, and alert search with towed sonar of unmanned surface vessel are studied. The work we done has practical significance, it can provide reference for submarine search equipment development and submarine search engineering application of unmanned surface vessel.

articleTitle: Predicting dynamic tensions of a moored semi-submersible fish farm by artificial neural network
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The reasonable design of mooring system is crucial to ensure the safety of offshore operation of a semisubmersible fish farm. Based on the three-dimensional potential flow theory, time-domain simulations are firstly conducted on a semi-submersible fish farm under actual sea conditions in the South China Sea. Then, a long short-term memory (LSTM) artificial neural network model is established to predict the mooring tensions. The prediction results are compared with the results of numerical simulations. It shows that the present model can well forecast the mooring tensions of a moored semi-submersible fish farm.

articleTitle: Collision risk assessment for floating nuclear power plants using a novel approach of Bayesian network and interval type-2 fuzzy sets
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Floating nuclear power plants (FNPPs) are an organic integration of smaller nuclear reactors and ship engineering, and there are currently no design codes related to FNPPs at home or abroad. Among them, ship collision is an important external event in the design of FNPPs, which has a significant impact on their safety. In order to solve the problem of collision risk faced by FNPPs, a risk analysis method is proposed using a combination of Bayesian network (BN) and interval type-2 fuzzy sets (IT2FS). The method adopts a fault tree to represent the hierarchical relationship of the risk system and maps it to a Bayesian network structure. IT2FS theory and expert evaluation are used to overcome the limitations of the lack of objective statistical data and incomplete knowledge, and the parameters of the fuzzy Bayesian network are determined based on a discrete aggregation method (DAM). In this work, taking China's first FNPP as a case study to validate the proposed approach, causal inference analysis, diagnostic inference analysis and sensitivity analysis are performed for the established fuzzy Bayesian network model enables the identification of key risk factors of collision. At the same time, targeted risk control measures are given to provide reference for on-site operation and management personnel.

articleTitle: Dynamic buckling analysis of hull structure under in-plane impact load
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The dynamic buckling of hull plates and stiffened plates under in-plane impact load was analyzed by the finite element method. The impact load was reasonably simplified and the correctness of the finite element analysis results was verified. For the hull plate, the influence of the load form, the load period, the initial deflection and the plate slenderness on the dynamic buckling was analyzed. For the stiffened plate, the influence of the load period, the plate slenderness, the stiffener slenderness and the initial deflection on the dynamic buckling was analyzed. The calculation formulae for the critical dynamic buckling load of the hull plates and stiffened plates were also obtained by the data of the finite element analyses. The proposed calculation formulae of critical dynamic buckling load of hull structure can be applied in the safe assessment of hull structure in Engineering.

articleTitle: Effects of sea level rise on storm tides in Zhoushan archipelago sea areas
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Climate change, such as sea level rise (SLR) and the intensification of typhoons, has significant influence on global storm surge intensity, thereby exacerbating coastal disasters. This study employs a numerical model coupling the tides, waves and storm tides to study the impacts of SLR on storm tides in Zhoushan archipelago sea areas. Taking Typhoon Chanhom as an example, the study ana-lyzes the impacts of SLR on storm tides. The findings show: (a) The SLR will reduce the total water level during storm tides. From the point of view of water level distribution, SLR will increase the water level of the East China Sea. (b) The SLR will strengthen the surge, which can reach 1m during the Chan-hom period. (c) The SLR will weaken the wave. In addition, the impact of SLR on the east-west direction of Yushan Island is small, and the impact on the north-south direction is greater.

articleTitle: High-resolution coastal flooding hazard assessment with pumping stations under climate change
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Due to climate change, coastal flooding poses a recurring threat to human lives and properties worldwide, resulting in substantial damages annually. Implementing well-balanced flood modelling is an efficient approach to accurately anticipate the dynamic nature of flooding, facilitating effective flood hazard management. Urban flood hazard management heavily relies on hydraulic structures, including but not limited to pumping stations, as they play a crucial part in mitigating flood impacts. A novel approach is introduced in this study, involving the integration of high-resolution coastal flood modelling and pumping stations to offer an object-level assessment of hazards in the face of climate change. The robustness of this new model is validated by applying it to reproduce Typhoon Lekima and further used to predict the future climate change impacts on critical infrastructures in Yuhuan, Zhejiang Province. At a resolution of 3m, quantitative hazard assessments are made to demonstrate the efficiency of the new high-resolution coastal flood model and the importance of directly considering pumping stations for reducing coastal flooding risk caused by climate change. After considering the pumping stations, more than half of the critical infrastructures escaped from the above medium risk level of vehicle instability.

articleTitle: Modeling the forced oscillations of a composite material cylinder in flow
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Modeling the vortex-induced vibration of the marine riser or marine umbilical cables is a challenge for the offshore platform analysis and design. More composite materials are used for the manufacture of marine riser in modern engineering. Classic model of cylinder is difficult to represent the time hysteresis of marine riser. In this paper, a generalized damping model that can represent the time hysteresis through the convolution integration is considered for the cylinder. The responses of a single degree of freedom of the cylinder with classic damping model or generalized damping model are computed for the comparison of the vibration amplitude. It turns out that the vibration amplitude of the cylinder with generalized damping model are larger than that of cylinder with classic viscous damping model. Thus, it is necessary to consider the time hysteresis of composite materials in the analysis of the vortex-induced vibration of marine riser.

articleTitle: Flow field identification method of underwater tracked vehicle based on artificial lateral line
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the local flow field of underwater equipment can not be measured in real-time, a flow field identification method of underwater tracked vehicle based on artificial lateral lines is proposed. Based on the artificial lateral line system and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation model of the tracked vehicle model, the pressure values of sensors with different inlet velocities and inlet angles are extracted. According to the distribution law of local flow field changes caused by a single variable, the pressure data of the artificial lateral line experiment and CFD simulation are integrated, and the flow field state matrix of tracked equipment is formed. After logarithmetics and normalization, the interpolation state matrix of equidistant sampling is mapped into an image. The datasets of inflow velocity, inflow angle, and obstacle location are constructed, and ResNet18 residual network is used to classify and identify the inflow velocity, inflow angle, and obstacle location of underwater tracked vehicle. The test recognition accuracy has reached 84%, which can meet the needs of underwater emergency rescue engineering.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of natural gas pipeline leakage and dispersion
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Natural gas is a kind of green and clean energy used as ship power. At the same time, natural gas is a flammable and explosive substances. It is important that the spread of natural gas after the leakage are analysed due to an unexpected accident. In this paper, CFD method is used to simulate the dispersion of natural gas in injection pipelines of LNG. The study focuses on comparing the distribution of natural gas in air under different wind speeds, wind directions, leak hole sizes, and leak directions. The computational results indicate that wind speed, wind direction, hole size, and leak direction are significant factors to affect the diffusion and concentration distribution of natural gas.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation and optimal design of the flow field in the cargo hold of an Antarctic krill ship
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Reasonable cold air flow field can ensure the uniformity of temperature field. In order to design the reasonable cold air flow field in the cargo hold of an Antarctic krill ship, the cold air flow field and temperature field in the cargo hold when it is empty are simulated numerically with fluent software. Based on the simulation results, the attitude and design parameters of the wind deflectors in the low-speed areas under the ventilated floor are adjusted, and two additional wind deflectors are added at the dead corners of air supply. Then the pressure field, velocity field and temperature field of the key profiles when the cargo hold is empty are simulated, and the simulated predicted values of the temperature field in the optimized cargo hold are compared with the measured values, and the two sets of data are found to be in good agreement. The research shows that the optimization scheme of this paper is not only helpful to solve the problem of unreasonable flow field distribution in the cargo hold of this Antarctic krill ship but also to improve its economy.

articleTitle: Structural design and theoretical simulation analysis of high-static-low-dynamic torsional vibration isolator for ship shafting
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: A torsional vibration isolator with high-static-low-dynamic stiffness (HSLDS) for ship shafting is proposed, which is designed based on axial parallel connection of positive stiffness and negative stiffness. Firstly, the geometric model is introduced, and then the model of HSLDS characteristic is verified by using FEM method. Secondly, the mechanical model is deduced by using harmonic balance method to analysis its harmonic response by numerical simulation. Finally, the torque transfer characteristics of HSLDS torsional vibration isolator is analyzed and compared to the typical linear isolator. Result shows that the isolator has good isolation characteristics of low frequency vibration with properly adjusting structural parameters.

articleTitle: Research on AIS and Radar based ship track fusion method
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Automatic Identification System (AIS) information and Radar data are important to ensure the safe operation of ships, as they are the most important sensing devices for ships during sea travel. This paper addresses the data fusion of AIS and Radar to improve the accuracy of the ship's dynamic perception of targets. After temporal alignment of the AIS and Radar data, based on the multi-target association problem encountered by ships during navigation, the accuracy of the track association is improved by combining with the neural network methods based on the double-threshold method to achieve more accurate object target tracking and identification. This is of some significance in ensuring the safe navigation of ships.

articleTitle: A multi-step prediction model of ship motion attitude based on chaos-LSTM
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Under the influence of multiple factors at sea, the ship will perform complex nonlinear swing. This will have a detrimental effect on ship operations at sea. To improve the accuracy of ship motion attitude prediction, a Chaos-LSTM based model is proposed based on the chaotic characteristics of the ship's sway. Firstly, the ship motion data is filtered by wavelet to remove the white noise. Secondly, the chaotic characteristics of the data are analyzed, the delay time τ and embedding dimension m are calculated. The data is then reconstructed in phase space and the reconstructed data is fed into the LSTM network. Finally, the prediction results are obtained and compared with EMD-LSTM and LSTM models. According to the experimental results based on the measured data, the Chaos-LSTM model is able to improve the reliability of the results, the established model has a certain generalization ability.

articleTitle: Analysis of wave spectrum characteristics in the pearl river estuary
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Based on the one-year wave data continuously collected at the Pearl River Estuary station, a statistical analysis of the wave spectrum characteristics was performed. In the comparison between the fitted Wen's spectrum and the measured spectrum in each season, the fitted spectrum has a slightly worse fitting effect in the the 0.5m group. For the other groups, especially those with larger wave heights, the fit is very good in terms of spectral peak sharpness and spectral shape. Comparing the seasonally fitted spectrum with the measured spectrum, the fitting effect of spectral fitting is poor for the relatively high wave group. For other groups, the effect on both peak sharpness and spectral shape fitting is better when the height wave is larger.During Typhoon 'Vicente', as the 'Vicente' is weaker, the peak of the wave spectrum is smaller and the peak frequency is concentrated in the high frequency region. When ocean condition is worse, the peak frequency of ocean wave spectrum is moving to the lower frequency part of the spectrum, with ocean wave energy would be focused on the lower frequency region. For the single peak spectrum of Typhoon 'Vicente', the fit is good for each group. There is a good fitting on the primary peak spectrum of the bimodal spectrum, but the Wen's spectra could not reflect the characteristics of the secondary peak spectrum, the error between observation and fitting of the bimodal spectrum is larger than the single peak spectrum.

articleTitle: Research on Fuzzy PID control for VOC oil vapor recovery system and dynamic fluctuations study
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of oil and gas recovery and treatment, better control the condensing temperature of the low-temperature heat exchanger, so that the exhaust gas and oil and gas recovery rate can meet the test requirements, this paper takes the low-temperature condensing oil and gas recovery platform as the research object, puts forward a control system with PLC as the core, and establishes the mathematical model of the low-temperature heat exchanger according to the test data. And Simulink toolbox in MATLAB software is used to simulate the control system of fuzzy PID and traditional PID, and the dynamic simulation of possible fluctuations is carried out. After comparing the analysis results, it is found that fuzzy PID control is more suitable for temperature control of low temperature system than traditional PID control. About 8 hours were saved in the experimental preparation engineering and 650L nitrogen was saved. Moreover, the control system can make the liquefaction process cope with the fluctuation condition well, so that the stability and safety of the test process can be improved, and the effective control of equipment operation can be realized.

articleTitle: The research on the underwater sound radiation noise caused by structure noise of single-layer cylindrical shell is important for the study of underwater noise pollution
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The stealth performance of submarines plays an important role in modern military warfare. The setting of its structure and the study of its acoustic radiation have especially important effects on the stealth performance of submarines. In the submarine structure, the cylinder shell structure is widely used as the main structural form of submarines and other similar military equipment. Therefore, this paper takes the cylinder shell as the research object and analyzes the acoustic radiation propagation rules in underwater environments based on statistical energy method through VA one simulation. Obtain the different attenuation effect of sound pressure level with distance and the influence of different composite structures on underwater noise through simulation analysis.

articleTitle: Near-wall effect of the large-scale immersed tunnel element under current loads
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The construction of a large-scale immersed tunnel is of great strategic significance to the utilization of underwater space and the establishment of a modern transportation system. Especially when approaching the bottom of the river or sea, the significant hydrodynamic interaction with the trench walls would affect the dynamic response of the tunnel element. Hence, in this study, a two-dimensional viscous CFD model is set to simulate the wall effect of this large-scale bluff body. The current loads acting on the immersed tunnel element are analyzed under various sinking and current velocities. It is observed that an increase in sinking velocity induces higher flow velocity between the bottom and the tunnel element and lower pressure on the top surface.

articleTitle: Acoustic characteristics analysis of sound insulation structure based on statistical energy method
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: In order to study the acoustic characteristics of sound insulation structure, taking the composite structure composed of steel plate and glass wool as an example, the calculation model of sound insulation structure is established by VA One, and the acoustic characteristics of the composite structure are solved by statistical energy method (SEA) and compared with the experimental values. The results show that in the frequency range of 125-4000Hz, the error between the simulated sound insulation of 2mm steel plate and 80mm glass wool composite structure and the experimental value is within 2dB. The simulation results are in good agreement with the experimental values, which verifies the accuracy of the statistical energy method and predicts the sound insulation performance of the double-layer glass.

articleTitle: Influence of particle damping (PDs) by controller the vibration reduction method based on acoustic black hole (ABH)
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Regarding applications in energy dissipation, transmission loss, vibration reduction, etc., there is a lot of hope for the Acoustics Black Hole (ABH) phenomenon. However, to significantly reduce vibration and maintain loss of dissipation energy, our research has learned to concentrate on the particle damping (PDs) used on the plate on the acoustic black hole (ABH-PDs). Fatigue damage is directly assessed in the frequency domain via the ABH structure characteristics modal model. The frequency domain finite element method (FEM) is used in this paper to successfully conduct our research by working in harmony with ABH structures. Our numerical and simulation work is carried out using various 2D and 3D simulation software (COMSOL Multiphysics and EDEM).

articleTitle: Research on ship coupled motion modeling in waves based on KT maneuvering response model
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Establishing accurate and reliable ship motion model is the key for high-precision prediction of ship oscillation and maneuvering motion. Based on the KT maneuvering response model, this paper adopts the modeling idea of double time scale model, and establishes a ship oscillation motion model according to three-dimensional potential flow theory, and proposes a new ship manipulative motion modeling method in waves. Based on the improved coupled motion model of ship waves, the maneuvering and oscillation motion prediction of ships in real waves are verified. The verification results show that the coupled motion model proposed in this paper can realize the high-precision prediction of ship maneuvering and oscillation motion.

articleTitle: Study on structural strength of all-aluminum multi-functional emergency high-speed sea patrol boat
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Because the structural design of aluminum alloy high-speed ship is more complicated than that of ordinary steel ship, the purpose of this paper is to ensure the structural safety of aluminum alloy high-speed ship. In this paper, an all-aluminum multi-functional emergency high-speed sea patrol boat is taken as the research object. MSC.Patran is used to model the whole ship by structural finite element method. After calculating and applying external loads, the analysis of yield stress results is completed, and the buckling plate is divided. MSC.Nastran is used to obtain the buckling stress cloud diagram, compare the location and distribution analysis of the maximum stress of the transverse and longitudinal components, and improve and optimize the structural characteristics of the high-speed boat. In this paper, a prediction method for the area where the structural strength of continuous structure needs to be strengthened is determined through research, and an elastic connection solution is proposed for the problem of insufficient deck buckling strength. By using the above two methods, this paper finally solves the problem of insufficient structural strength in the actual production of the ship, and provides a design basis for the subsequent development of this type of ship.

articleTitle: Influence of perforated wall on loading of OWC caisson under action of dam-break waves
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The weather-side thin wall of oscillating water column (OWC) caisson is relatively weak and prone to structural damage under extreme sea conditions, as evidenced by the damage of several prototypes. Perforated wall is often employed for coastal protection due to feature of wave energy dissipation, which may result in a lower wave reflection and reduced wave loads. This study investigates the influence of perforated walls on the wave loading on the OWC caisson. A viscous-flow-based numerical model is developed to simulate dam-break waves interacting with OWC caisson and is validated against experimental data. The wave force and distributed wave pressure on the caisson wall are presented. Numerical results indicate that perforated wall effectively buffer the transient impact energy of the dam-break wave. The perforated wall significantly reduces wave loading on the OWC caisson, with observed quantitative reductions of up to 80%. In addition, the details of the three-dimensional impacts are illustrated.

articleTitle: Intelligent transformation and upgrading of shipment industry: ``force field analysis'' and advancement strategies
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: With the advent of the information age, the traditional shipping industry is facing the challenge of intelligent transformation and upgrading. The intelligent transformation of the shipping industry includes four typical construction tasks: ship intelligence, port intelligence, intelligent shipping logistics supply chain, and intelligent shipping services. The intelligent transformation and upgrading of the shipping industry face both strong driving forces and significant resistance. Based on the force field analysis of the intelligent transformation of the shipping industry, effective promotion of intelligent transformation in the shipping industry requires the continuous strengthening of driving forces while weakening resistance. This can be achieved by designing an intelligent transformation path from five aspects: ``source force, driving force, supporting force, propelling force, and leading force,'' and empowering the intelligent transformation of the shipping industry through the ``Five Forces.''

articleTitle: Study on compiling water load spectrum for take off and landing of amphibious aircraft based on task analysis method
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The amphibious aircraft generally uses the form of hull water dynamic layout, carrying the forest fire fighting, sea rescue and other special operation tasks, and needs to frequently take off and land on the water surface. However, it bears complex water dynamic loads in the process of takeoff and landing, and the existence of these loads will cause the dynamic response of the aircraft structure. The compilation of load spectrum plays a very important role in designing the structural fatigue, damage tolerance and service life of designing amphibious aircraft. In this paper, the water load spectrum is defined as the center of gravity overload spectrum of the amphibious aircraft taking off and landing on the water surface, mainly studies the use characteristics of the amphibious aircraft for takeoff and landing on the surface of the water plane, according to the typical mission profile of the amphibious aircraft. The task analysis method, which is the basic method of spectrum compilation, is used to establish the compilation method of water surface precipitation load spectrum of amphibious aircraft, and the implementation steps of this method are described.

articleTitle: Preliminary analysis on the influence of sand pit on the integrity of offshore pipeline
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Due to the sand mining activities, the boundary of the sand pit continuously expands to an in-service offshore pipeline, which poses a great threat to the integrity of the pipeline. In order to ensure the integrity of the pipeline during operation, a comprehensive scheme of "monitoring - assessment- classification- treatment" is proposed in this paper. Through the survey, the boundary characteristics of sand pit are obtained as the basis for further analysis. The study finds that extreme weather, particularly typhoons, significantly influences seabed slope changes. The stability of sand pit slope is analysed based on the surveyed seabed topography, and a method for assessing risk levels using the critical slope stability angle is introduced. Furthermore, the paper summarizes control measures implemented in the project, discusses solutions for areas with varying risk levels, and presents an integrity assurance method for submarine pipelines near sand pits, which relies on monitoring and numerical calculations.

articleTitle: Comparative numerical investigation of collision applying unorthodox modified Y profile ship structures
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: This paper intends to investigate unorthodox alternative hulls to mitigate impacts of ship collision accidents. Collision of ships may cause severe drawbacks to the marine environment as well as marine transportation. The investigation is thus concentrating on analysis of unorthodox modified Y profile hulls compared to a conventional datum hull from established literatures. The modified sections are composed of shaped stiffeners equivalent to the standard longitudinals with minimum weight but having equal or higher section modulus. The crashworthiness of the modified hulls compared to the datum hull is ascertained through their energy dissipation abilities and strength in terms of resisting impact forces. The unorthodox modified Y sections are found to improve the collision energy capacity and the strength of inner hulls maintaining watertight integrity, consequently, can be adopted to reduce the impacts and hazards from ship collisions. Moreover, they can improve marine transportation safety and marine environmental protection via more crashworthy hull structures. When carefully designed and optimized, unorthodox Y profiles can be made lighter resulting into lighter hull but yet crashworthy structures.

articleTitle: Establishment of the "three lines" coastal control model: a case study of Taizhou city
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: The "three lines" of the coastal zone refer to the coastline, development setback control lines and development restriction lines. In this paper, the distance of development setback control line is determined by constructing a model of calculating the distance of development setback control line through human settlement environment index and resource exploitation intensity index. The development limit line was defined by calculating five factors: coastal resource utilization intensity, environmental element response, ecological index response, degree of resource and environmental protection and regional economic development status. The model was applied in Taizhou City, Zhejiang Province, The results show that: (1) The "three line" control model of coastal region determines the development and protection boundaries of land and sea, which provides technical support for the suitable allocation of coastal resources. (2) The distance of development setback control lines in each district of Taizhou is 619.5m for Sanmen, 507.7m for Wenling, 501.6m for Luqiao, 253.1m for Jiaojiang, 197.1m for Yuhuan and 141.4m for Linhai. (3) The development limit distance of Jiaojiang, Linhai and Luqiao is 3,936 m, Yuhuan is 5,904m, Wenling and Sanmen is 7,872m.

articleTitle: Integrated navigation method of human-occupied vehicle based on linear regression and adaptive unscented Kalman filter
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of large navigation errors caused by multiple sensor measurements with different rates in the integrated navigation system, a new integrated navigation method for Human Occupied Vehicles (HOV) is put forward. The integrated navigation method consists of linear regression (LR) and adaptive unscented Kalman filter (AUKF). The LR prediction model is proposed in this paper, which can predict the ultra-short baseline (USBL) data with update intervals, then increase the effective date in the USBL data set. Then, AUKF is used to fuse multi-sensor data to obtain an accurate location of HOV. Finally, the performance of LR-AUKF is verified by simulation experiments with the real navigation data of Jiao long HOV. The simulation experimental results demonstrate.

articleTitle: Based on the ship power spectrum method preparation of seaplane water load spectrum
publicationTitle: International Joint Conference on Civil and Marine Engineering (JCCME 2023)
abstract: Seaplanes bear complex hydrodynamic loads during takeoff and landing in different waters. It is of great guiding significance for the design and manufacture of seaplanes to master the variation of water load in different mission scenarios and to use appropriate methods to compile water load spectrum. In view of the lack of measured data of similar seaplane when compiling water load spectrum for seaplanes, the method of calculating water load spectrum based on power spectrum is studied: According to the meaningful wave height and overload increment of the model pool test, the corresponding amplitude operator of the real machine is calculated, and the wave spectrum of the target water area is input. The overload incremental power spectrum of the real seaplane is obtained through spectral analysis. Then the power spectrum method is used to calculate the overpass times of each overload increment, and the gravity overload spectrum of seaplane in different task situations is obtained, which reflects the change of water load during the seaplane mission. And the STAR-CCM+ software was used to calculate and analyze the load and motion response of the seaplane during landing and gliding at a certain speed and attitude angle, in order to verify the reliability of the research method.
